svg.text: Load against a 3-node Raft cluster, with the #5492 materialized-view A/B

g.text: count by scan as well as by index
count by scan as well as by index
log markers, not just row counts
log markers, not just row counts
a full scan reads the buckets
both must give the same number
Load against HA: the cluster is started, a leader is awaited, and the schema is created on that leader.
Every node must answer the schema query before any load starts, and the wait is measured, not slept.
db1/db2/db3.awaitSchema(60) - plus awaitMaterializedView(60) in the view arm - elapsed ms is logged
Every writer targets the leader directly, so the run measures replication rather than request forwarding.
3 x addUserAndPhotos(1000, 10) on leaderServer; friendships and likes are configured to 0 in this test
The polling loop reads all three nodes at once, so divergence shows up in the log as it happens.
Convergence is awaited on equality, then each node is asserted against the absolute expected totals.
awaitConvergence(...) atMost 2 min, then per node: users 3000, photos 30000, friendships 0, likes 0
Every node is counted a second time by scanning the type, because an index and a scan can disagree.
assertThatScannedCountIs("User", 3000) and ("Photo", 30000) on db1, db2 and db3
A second method repeats the identical run with a REFRESH INCREMENTAL view, the only difference between the arms.
threeNodeReplicationWithMaterializedView() is @Tag("slow"), HTTP only; the view must converge non-empty on every node
Container logs are scanned afterwards: counts alone cannot tell a clean run from one that diverged and resynced.
counts "does not match with existent version", "triggering snapshot resync", "Snapshot resync completed" + a canary marker
